docs.title: frzspatial
docs.text:
CosMx (AtoMx) exports to SpatialData, for TMA slides: fast loading and caching, cores stitched into one image, plots, and hand annotation of regions in napari that ends up as a cell-level column.

  • Read an AtoMx flat-file export (counts, metadata, polygons, transcripts, per-FOV composites and masks) into one SpatialData object in AtoMx global pixels: in parallel, with transcripts cached as Parquet and images read lazily.
  • Reopen saved slides in seconds (load_slides), building only the missing ones, with a progress bar.
  • Stitch a TMA core, or a whole slide at reduced resolution, into one composite and one mask layer for napari (build_core).
  • Plot a slide overview or one core with its outlines, transcripts or any obs column (frzspatial.pl).
  • Annotate regions (glomeruli, arteries, ...) or single cells in napari; polygons are saved as GeoJSON after every change and each cell gets the class of the polygon around its centroid (annotate_core, annotations_to_obs).
  • QC: regional signal-to-background ratio per cell (compute_sbr).
  • Register a whole-slide H&E onto the cells from tissue shape alone (frzspatial.he).
  • Export count matrices and metadata as plain files for a Seurat object in R (write_seurat_inputs).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install "git+https://github.com/franzake/frzspatial"

This installs everything: plotting (spatialdata-plot), napari with PyQt5, and H&E registration (scikit-image).

From R with reticulate:

reticulate::py_require("frzspatial @ git+https://github.com/franzake/frzspatial")

It installs from wheels only (nothing to compile) on Linux, Windows and macOS 14+, with Python 3.12 to 3.14:

  • Intel Macs: numba and llvmlite are kept at 0.62 / 0.45, the last versions with Intel Mac wheels. Use Python 3.12 or 3.13 there: numba has no Intel Mac wheels for Python 3.14.
  • napari stays < 0.10, the last versions that work with PyQt5. On ARM Linux, where PyQt5 has no wheels, napari is installed without a Qt backend (pip install pyqt6 to open windows).

Tested with Python 3.12, spatialdata 0.8.0, spatialdata-plot 0.4.3, napari 0.9.2 and napari-spatialdata 0.7.2.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import frzspatial as fs

# Each slide's export is in data/<slide>_inputs/ (flatFiles/, CellComposite/, CellLabels/)
slides = fs.load_slides(["MN2", "MN3"], input_dir="data", zarr_dir="data/zarr", cache_dir="data/cache")
sdata = slides["MN2"]

The first call builds and saves data/zarr/MN2_flat.zarr (minutes); later calls only open it (seconds).

Cores need an obs column with each cell's core name (core_str by default) and, for annotations, its slide name (slide):

obs = sdata.tables["table"].obs
obs["slide"] = "MN2"
obs["core_str"] = ...  # e.g. from your TMA key

# Plots
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from frzspatial.pl import plot_core, plot_slide_overview

plot_slide_overview(sdata, "core_str"); plt.show()
plot_core(sdata, "C4R7", genes={"NPHS2": "magenta", "LRP2": "orange"}); plt.show()

# napari: one core at full resolution, or the whole slide (core=None) at 1/8
from frzspatial.viewer import open_napari
open_napari(fs.build_core(sdata, "MN2", "C4R7"))

docs.title: Annotating regions
docs.text:
from frzspatial.viewer import annotate_core
from frzspatial.pl import annotation_palette, plot_core

CLASSES = ["Glomerulus", "Sclerotic_glomerulus", "Tubulointerstitium", "Artery", "Inflammation", "Exclude"]
annotate_core(sdata, "MN2", "C4R7", CLASSES)     # opens napari; returns when the window is closed

obs = sdata.tables["table"].obs
obs["manual_annotation"].value_counts()
plot_core(sdata, "C4R7", color="manual_annotation", palette=annotation_palette(CLASSES, obs["manual_annotation"]))

fs.save_table(sdata)                             # store the new column in MN2_flat.zarr

In napari, click the annot: <class> layer of a class, then draw:

To do How draw a region P (polygon), click around it, double-click to close mark single cells zoom in, R (rectangle), drag a small box over the cell's centre move or delete a shape 5 (select), click it, then drag or press Backspace colour the outlines select cell_boundaries, pick a column in the View panel

Each change is saved to results/annotations/<slide>_<core>.geojson. Close the window with its own close button. When Python runs inside R or Jupyter, don't quit with Cmd-Q: it quits the host's Qt loop and can hang it, and force-quitting the window kills the host. Rerunning annotate_core on the same core reopens its shapes for editing; fs.annotations_to_obs(sdata, CLASSES) rebuilds the column from the files at any time.

docs.title: Merged slides
docs.text:
After spatialdata.concatenate with each slide's elements suffixed -<slide> and in coordinate system global-<slide>, the same functions take the merged object and a slide name:

open_napari(fs.build_core(merged, "MN2", "C4R7", colors={"cell_type": {"Podocyte": "#e377c2", ...}}))
fs.annotations_to_obs(merged, CLASSES)  # every slide's files, matched on obs["slide"] and obs["core_str"]

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
frzspatial build data/MN2_inputs MN2 -o MN2_flat.zarr --cache-dir cache
frzspatial info MN2_flat.zarr
frzspatial view MN2_flat.zarr --slide MN2 --core C4R7
frzspatial view MN2_flat.zarr --slide MN2 --core C4R7 --annotate Glomerulus Artery

frzspatial <command> --help lists every option.

docs.title: Help
docs.text: Every function has a docstring: help(fs.build_core), or fs.build_core? in IPython. The module docstrings (help(frzspatial.io), help(frzspatial.core)) describe the expected export layout and coordinate systems. The full reference is at https://franzake.github.io/frzspatial, or build it locally with pip install "frzspatial[docs]" && mkdocs serve.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Positions are AtoMx global px (0.120280945 µm/px, fs.PX_UM); each FOV is placed with x = dx + col, y = cy - row, so FOVs stitch without resampling.
  • Cells are named by AtoMx's cell (c_<slide_ID>_<fov>_<cell_ID>).
  • fs.set_verbose(False) silences the progress messages.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/franzake/frzspatial && cd frzspatial
pip install -e ".[test,docs]"
pytest

The tests build a small synthetic AtoMx export, so they need no data.

docs.title: Annotation in napari
docs.text:
1. Open the slide and make sure its table has the slide and core_str obs columns.
  2. Run annotate_core(sdata, slide, core, classes) (core=None for the whole slide, at 1/8 resolution). napari opens with the core's composite, its cell outlines and one empty layer annot: <class> per class. Shapes saved for this core earlier are loaded back.
  3. Click the layer of a class and draw: P for a polygon (double-click to close), R for a rectangle (a small one over a cell's centre marks a single cell), 5 to select, move or delete. Ellipses are ignored.
  4. Every change is saved to <annot_dir>/<slide>_<core>.geojson, in the slide's global px.
  5. Close the window with its own close button (not Cmd-Q when Python runs inside R or Jupyter). The polygon count is printed and obs["manual_annotation"] is rebuilt from every file in annot_dir.
  6. Check it with obs["manual_annotation"].value_counts() or plot_core(sdata, core, color="manual_annotation", palette=annotation_palette(classes, obs["manual_annotation"])).
  7. Store the column in the slide's zarr with save_table(sdata).

Each cell takes the class of the polygon that contains its centroid; where polygons overlap, the class later in classes wins. The column is categorical with every class as a category, so tables annotated separately still share their categories when they are concatenated.

If napari hangs or the host process dies, nothing drawn is lost: rerun annotate_core to reopen the shapes, or annotations_to_obs(sdata, classes) to rebuild the column.

docs.title: Reading and saving
docs.text:
Read CosMx AtoMx flat-file exports into SpatialData, in AtoMx global pixels.

An AtoMx export folder (<inputs>) is expected to look like::

<inputs>/
  flatFiles/<id>_metadata_file.csv[.gz]
  flatFiles/<id>_exprMat_file.csv[.gz]
  flatFiles/<id>-polygons.csv[.gz]
  flatFiles/<id>_tx_file.csv[.gz]
  CellComposite/CellComposite_F00001.jpg ...
  CellLabels/CellLabels_F00001.tif ...
  Morphology2D/*_F00001.TIF ...              (optional)

where <id> is the dataset id (usually the slide name). :func:build_sdata turns it into one SpatialData object with these elements, all in the "global" coordinate system:

===================== ============================================================================== table counts (sparse int32) and cell metadata; cells named by cell (c_<slide>_<fov>_<id>) cell_boundaries one polygon per cell transcripts lazy points from a Parquet cache (x, y, z_raw, target, cell, CellComp, fov) fov<N>_image CellComposite of each FOV (lazy) fov<N>_labels CellLabels mask of each FOV (lazy) fov<N>_morphology Morphology2D of each FOV, one channel per marker (optional, lazy) ===================== ==============================================================================

Each FOV is placed with x_global = x_local + dx and y_global = cy - y_local (image row = y_local).

Speed: gzip is decompressed by pigz in a separate process when it is installed, CSVs are parsed by multithreaded pyarrow, transcripts are streamed to Parquet once (reused while newer than the CSV) and read lazily, and table, polygons and transcripts are read in parallel.

docs.title: build_sdata(inputs, cache_dir, dataset_id, *, images=True, morphology=False, transcripts=True, threads=8, flip_y=True)
docs.text:
Build one SpatialData object from an AtoMx export folder.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default inputs

Export folder holding flatFiles/, CellComposite/ and CellLabels/ (see the module docs).

required cache_dir

Folder for the transcript Parquet cache (<dataset_id>_tx.parquet).

required dataset_id

Prefix of the flat files, usually the slide name.

required images

Read the per-FOV composites and masks (lazily).

True morphology

Also read Morphology2D/ as fov<N>_morphology (one channel per marker).

False transcripts

Read the transcripts (via the Parquet cache).

True threads

Threads for pigz and the CSV parser.

8 flip_y

Add the "slide" coordinate system, y upwards (:func:add_slide_view).

True

Returns:

Type Description SpatialData

Lazy where possible: write it with sdata.write(path) and reopen it with :func:load_slides or spatialdata.read_zarr.

Examples:

>>> sdata = build_sdata("data/MN2_inputs", cache_dir="cache", dataset_id="MN2")
>>> sdata.write("MN2_flat.zarr")

docs.title: load_slides(slides, input_dir, zarr_dir, cache_dir, *, rebuild=False, morphology=False)
docs.text:
Open several slides, building the missing ones.

Each slide is reopened from <zarr_dir>/<slide>_flat.zarr. A slide without a zarr is first built from <input_dir>/<slide>_inputs with :func:build_sdata and saved there.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default slides

Slide names, also used as the flat files' dataset ids.

required input_dir

Folder holding the <slide>_inputs export folders.

required zarr_dir

Folder of the <slide>_flat.zarr files.

required cache_dir

Transcript Parquet cache, as in :func:build_sdata.

required rebuild

True rebuilds every slide; a list rebuilds only those.

False morphology

Passed to :func:build_sdata.

False

Returns:

Type Description dict

{slide: SpatialData}. Images and masks are read lazily from the zarr.

Notes

ome_zarr's "no parent found" warnings (one per FOV mask, harmless) are silenced.

docs.title: save_table(sdata, table='table')
docs.text:
Write sdata's table back into the zarr it was read from (e.g. after adding obs columns).

spatialdata does not overwrite an element of its own backing zarr, so the table is deleted on disk and written again; images, masks, polygons and transcripts on disk are left unchanged. Takes seconds per slide. Do not interrupt it: between the two steps the zarr has no table.

docs.title: add_slide_view(sdata, name='slide')
docs.text:
Add a coordinate system name: "global" mirrored in y (y = y_max - y_global).

spatialdata-plot draws y downwards (the image convention); in this system plots show y upwards, as in the AtoMx slide view. "global" itself is left unchanged. Modifies sdata in place and returns it.

docs.title: Cores
docs.text:
Cores of a TMA slide: their bounding box and a stitched, napari-ready SpatialData per core or slide.

Two kinds of objects are supported everywhere:

  • a single slide (e.g. one value of :func:frzspatial.load_slides): unsuffixed elements (fov<N>_image, cell_boundaries, transcripts) in the coordinate system "global";
  • a merged object (several slides concatenated with spatialdata.concatenate): each slide's elements suffixed -<slide> and in their own coordinate system "global-<slide>", so slides never overlap.

docs.title: coordinate_system(sdata, slide)
docs.text: ("-<slide>", "global-<slide>") for a merged object, ("", "global") for a single slide.

docs.title: core_box(sdata, core, core_key='core_str', table='table')
docs.text:
Bounding-box query arguments for one core of a single slide: the rectangle around its cells.

Use as sdata.query.bounding_box(**core_box(sdata, "C4R7")).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If no cell has obs[core_key] == core.

docs.title: build_core(sdata, slide, core=None, table='table', colors=None, scale_factors=(2, 2, 2), downsample=None, core_key='core_str', slide_key='slide')
docs.text:
One core, or a whole slide, as a small SpatialData object for napari.

The core's FOVs are stitched into one composite and one mask layer. FOVs are placed by their AtoMx offsets (x = col + dx, y = cy - row) in integer px, so stitching needs no resampling.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sdata

A single slide or a merged object (see the module docs).

required slide

Slide name: selects the elements and coordinate system of a merged object, and the cells with obs[slide_key] == slide.

required core

Core name (obs[core_key]), or None for the whole slide.

None table

Table element name.

'table' colors

{column: {category: colour}}, stored as the table's <column>_colors: napari-spatialdata only colours a categorical column reliably with them.

None scale_factors

Pyramid of the image and masks: each level halves.

(2, 2, 2) downsample

Keep every n-th pixel of each FOV (the transformation scales it back to the slide's px). Default 1 for a core and 8 for a whole slide (a full-resolution slide is ~40 GB of RGB).

None core_key

obs columns of the core and slide names (slide_key is only used for a merged object).

'core_str' slide_key

obs columns of the core and slide names (slide_key is only used for a merged object).

'core_str'

Returns:

Type Description SpatialData

core_image (multiscale RGB), core_labels (each cell's mask value = its integer id in the table and polygons), cell_boundaries, transcripts and table (only cells with a polygon, as napari needs one shape per row; unused categories dropped; the original names in obs["cell_name"]), in the slide's coordinate system. Needs obs["fov"] and obs["slide_ID"].

Examples:

>>> from frzspatial.viewer import open_napari
>>> open_napari(build_core(slides["MN2"], "MN2", "C4R7"))

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text:
Hand annotations: polygons saved as GeoJSON, turned into a cell-level obs column.

Annotations are stored one file per core in an annotation folder, named <slide>_<core>.geojson (<slide>_slide.geojson for shapes drawn on a whole slide), with one class property per polygon and coordinates in the slide's global px. They are drawn with :func:frzspatial.viewer.annotate_core, but any GeoJSON in that layout works (e.g. exported from QuPath after converting to global px).

This module does not need napari.

docs.title: annotation_file(annot_dir, slide, core=None)
docs.text: Path of a core's annotation file: <annot_dir>/<slide>_<core>.geojson (core None: <slide>_slide).

docs.title: read_annotations(path)
docs.text:
Polygons of one annotation file as a GeoDataFrame (class, geometry), one row per polygon.

A missing file gives an empty GeoDataFrame; multipolygons are split into polygons.

docs.title: write_annotations(annot, path)
docs.text: Save polygons (GeoDataFrame with class and geometry) to path; an empty one deletes the file.

docs.title: annotations_to_obs(sdata, classes, annot_dir='results/annotations', column='manual_annotation', table='table', slide_key='slide', core_key='core_str')
docs.text:
Label each cell with the class of the annotated polygon around its centroid.

Every <slide>_<core>.geojson in annot_dir is applied to the cells with obs[slide_key] == slide and obs[core_key] == core (all cells of the slide for <slide>_slide.geojson). Files of slides or cores not in the table are skipped, so the same folder can serve each slide and a merged object.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sdata

A single slide or a merged object.

required classes

Class names in priority order: where polygons overlap, the class later in the list wins.

required annot_dir

Folder of the GeoJSON files.

'results/annotations' column

obs column to write.

'manual_annotation' table

Table element and its obs columns of slide and core names. Positions are CenterX/Y_global_px.

'table' slide_key

Table element and its obs columns of slide and core names. Positions are CenterX/Y_global_px.

'table' core_key

Table element and its obs columns of slide and core names. Positions are CenterX/Y_global_px.

'table'

Returns:

Type Description Series

Cells per class. obs[column] is set in place: categorical with every class as a category (used or not, so that tables annotated separately still share them when merged), NA outside every polygon.

Examples:

>>> annotations_to_obs(slides["MN2"], ["Glomerulus", "Artery"])
Glomerulus    126
Artery          0

docs.title: QC
docs.text: Per-cell QC of a SpatialData table.

docs.title: compute_sbr(sdata, bandwidth=0.01, weight_cutoff=0.08, bg_quantile=0.01, sbr_min=0, sbr_max=None, table='table', label='')
docs.text:
Regional signal-to-background ratio (SBR) of each cell.

Mean gene counts over mean negative-probe counts, each smoothed over the cell's neighbours with Gaussian weights. Same algorithm and defaults as computeSBR() in Barisano's CosMx QC (R).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sdata

A SpatialData object whose table has CenterX/Y_global_px and probes named Negative* (negative probes) and SystemControl* (excluded).

required bandwidth

Gaussian bandwidth, mm.

0.01 weight_cutoff

Neighbours with a smaller weight are ignored (sets the search radius).

0.08 bg_quantile

The smoothed background is floored at this quantile of its positive values: a near-zero background otherwise gives ratios of ~1e9.

0.01 sbr_min

Bounds on log2(SBR) for flag_sbr; None disables a bound.

0 sbr_max

Bounds on log2(SBR) for flag_sbr; None disables a bound.

0 table

Table element name.

'table' label

Prefix of the printed summary (e.g. the slide name).

''

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

SBR per cell. obs gets SBR, log2SBR and flag_sbr in place.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
Static plots of single slides with spatialdata-plot, y up as in the AtoMx slide view.

Each function returns the matplotlib axes without showing them: call plt.show() or ax.figure.savefig(...).

docs.title: plot_slide_overview(sdata, color, title=None, figsize=(12, 20), dpi=200, fontsize=8)
docs.text:
All cells of a single slide coloured by an obs column, each group labelled at its median position.

Cells are rasterised by datashader at figsize × dpi pixels: at ~1000 px across a slide one pixel is about one cell, so raise dpi for sharper cores.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sdata

A single slide.

required color

obs column, e.g. "core_str" or "fov".

required title

Plot title (default: color).

None figsize

Figure size (inches) and resolution.

(12, 20) dpi

Figure size (inches) and resolution.

(12, 20) fontsize

Size of the group labels.

8

docs.title: plot_core(sdata, core, genes=None, color=None, palette=None, title=None, core_key='core_str')
docs.text:
One core of a single slide: its composite image, cell outlines and selected transcripts.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sdata

A single slide.

required core

Core name (obs[core_key]).

required genes

{gene: colour} of transcripts to draw.

None color

obs column to fill the cells by (e.g. "manual_annotation"); without it, cells are outlined in yellow.

None palette

{value: colour} for color; cells with other values or NA are left unfilled.

None title

Plot title (default: core).

None

Examples:

>>> plot_core(slides["MN2"], "C4R7", genes={"NPHS2": "magenta"})
>>> plot_core(slides["MN2"], "C4R7", color="manual_annotation",
...           palette=annotation_palette(classes))

docs.title: annotation_palette(classes, used=None)
docs.text:
{class: colour} in the colours of :func:frzspatial.viewer.annotate_core's layers (scanpy's default_20).

used: an obs column; only the classes that occur in it are returned (for :func:plot_core's palette).

docs.title: napari
docs.text:
napari windows: view a SpatialData object, and draw annotations on a core or slide.

Importing this module loads Qt, so import it only where a window is opened.

Notes

When Python runs inside another program (R through reticulate, Jupyter), the napari window belongs to that program: close it with the window's own close button. Quitting with Cmd-Q quits the host application's Qt loop and can hang it, and force-quitting the window kills the host (e.g. the R session). Annotations are saved after every change, so a hang loses nothing.

docs.title: patch_anndata()
docs.text: Restore AnnData._get_X, removed in anndata 0.13 but still called by napari-spatialdata 0.7 (colour by gene). Called by :func:open_napari and :func:annotate_core; call it yourself before opening napari-spatialdata another way.

docs.title: open_napari(sdata)
docs.text:
Show sdata in a napari-spatialdata window; returns when the window is closed.

The window can open behind other windows (look for it with Cmd-Tab / Alt-Tab).

Examples:

>>> open_napari(build_core(slides["MN2"], "MN2", "C4R7"))

docs.title: annotate_core(sdata, slide, core, classes, annot_dir='results/annotations', column='manual_annotation', colors=None, table='table', downsample=None)
docs.text:
Draw regions on a core (or a whole slide) in napari, one layer per class; label the cells on closing.

The core is stitched by :func:frzspatial.build_core and opened with its composite, cell outlines (not for a whole slide: ~70k outlines are slow) and one Shapes layer annot: <class> per class, holding this core's saved polygons. Draw polygons (P) or rectangles (R) in the layer of a class; ellipses are ignored. Each change is saved to <annot_dir>/<slide>_<core>.geojson (global px). When the window is closed, obs[column] is rebuilt from every saved file (:func:frzspatial.annotations_to_obs).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sdata

A single slide or a merged object.

required slide

Slide name.

required core

Core name, or None for the whole slide (downsampled; saved to <slide>_slide.geojson).

required classes

Class names, in priority order for overlaps; classes found only in the saved file are added.

required annot_dir

As in :func:frzspatial.annotations_to_obs.

'results/annotations' column

As in :func:frzspatial.annotations_to_obs.

'results/annotations' table

As in :func:frzspatial.annotations_to_obs.

'results/annotations' colors

As in :func:frzspatial.build_core.

None downsample

As in :func:frzspatial.build_core.

None

Returns:

Type Description GeoDataFrame

The core's polygons (class, geometry).

docs.title: H&E registration
docs.text: Register a whole-slide H&E (Aperio SVS) onto the CosMx cells, from tissue shape alone.

docs.title: register_he(cells_px, he_overview, he_um_per_overview_px, px_um=PX_UM, grid_um=50, min_blob_mm2=0.05)
docs.text:
Fit the CosMx → H&E transform from tissue shape alone.

  1. Tissue masks on a grid_um grid: the H&E by Otsu threshold, the cells by occupancy.
  2. Rigid search: the 8 right-angle rotations and flips, then a ±4° sweep, each with its best translation by FFT cross-correlation (pixel sizes are known, so the scale is fixed).
  3. Landmarks: each tissue blob (e.g. a TMA core) fully covered by cells is paired with its H&E blob; with at least 3 pairs, outliers are dropped and the affine is refitted on their centroids.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cells_px

(n, 2) cell centroids in global px.

required he_overview

A coarse H&E level, (y, x, 3).

required he_um_per_overview_px

µm per pixel of he_overview.

required px_um

µm per CosMx global px.

PX_UM grid_um

Mask grid, µm.

50 min_blob_mm2

Smallest blob used as a landmark, mm².

0.05

Returns:

Name Type Description affine Affine

H&E µm → global px.

pairs DataFrame

Landmark pairs (x_px, y_px, he_x_um, he_y_um, resid_um).

score float

Fraction of the cells' tissue on H&E tissue.

docs.title: add_he_image(sdata, svs, name='he', px_um=PX_UM, grid_um=50)
docs.text:
Add a whole-slide H&E (Aperio SVS) as a lazy multiscale image, registered onto the cells.

The SVS's own pyramid levels become the scales, so nothing is read until plotted or written, except the coarsest level, used by :func:register_he. The pixel size comes from the SVS header (MPP). Landmark pairs are kept as shapes <name>_landmarks (H&E) and cell_landmarks.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sdata

A single slide, e.g. from :func:frzspatial.build_sdata. Modified in place and returned.

required svs

Path of the SVS file.

required name

Image element name.

'he'

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
Export for R/Seurat without conversion packages.

:func:write_seurat_inputs writes plain files that R reads directly. A matching R reader::

read_csc = function(dir, assay, genes, cells) {
  i = readBin(file.path(dir, paste0(assay, "_i.bin")), "integer", n = 2^31 - 1)
  p = readBin(file.path(dir, paste0(assay, "_p.bin")), "integer", n = length(cells) + 1)
  x = readBin(file.path(dir, paste0(assay, "_x.bin")), "double", n = length(i))
  Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = i, p = p, x = x, index1 = FALSE, dims = c(length(genes), length(cells)),
                       dimnames = list(genes, cells))
}
